title: Version Safeguard Registry and Rolling Upgrade Playbook for Private VPC Modules
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a Version Safeguard Registry (VSR) and a rolling upgrade playbook for Terraform modules and providers used by Redwood Private (VPC) deployments. The goal is to reduce upgrade-induced incidents during provider or module upgrades, make pinning decisions explicit and auditable, and automate pre-upgrade health checks and post-upgrade validation.

Background and problem statement:
- We’ve observed multiple incidents during provider/module upgrades where implicit provider compatibility allowed drift (e.g., minor provider changes that alter resource defaults, or module refactors that rely on newer provider behavior).
- Current pinning is ad-hoc across repos; there is no single source of truth for safe provider+module combinations for each supported Terraform runtime (e.g., 1.4.x, 1.5.x).
- Upgrades are performed manually in several customer/private repos, increasing risk. We need a registry, CI gates, and an automated rolling upgrade playbook that can be executed by platform SREs or triggered from Dedicated/Private upgrade pipelines.

Objectives:
1) Create a machine-readable Version Safeguard Registry (VSR) stored in the platform infra repo that enumerates tested module/provider combinations per terraform runtime and per cloud provider.
2) Define clear pinning policies (when to pin exactly vs. allow patch upgrades) and a deprecation signal mechanism for module/provider versions approaching end-of-support.
3) Implement a CI workflow that validates PRs that change provider/module constraints against the VSR plus a staged upgrade job that can execute canary applies and health checks.
4) Document a human readable rolling upgrade playbook for platform operators, including rollback criteria and post-upgrade validations.

Rationale for uniqueness of approach:
- Instead of a single global pin file, the VSR will be scoped by "environment profile" (hosted/dedicated/private) and by customer class when needed. This reduces unnecessary lock-in for hosted while preserving stability guarantees for private customers with stricter compliance needs.
- The registry will include metadata: tested_tf_version, tested_provider_versions, test-commit-sha, last_tested_date, compatibility_level (green/amber/red), recommended_action (pin/allow-patch/upgrade-with-canary).

Expected deliverables:
- VSR JSON schema and initial content covering aws, azurerm, google, and kubernetes providers plus our common modules (network, compute, storage, iam).
- CI-based validation job (GH Actions) that rejects PRs not aligned with VSR or that attempt upgrades without an associated upgrade job.
- Playbook markdown for rolling upgrades with prescriptive canary percentages, health checks, and rollback steps.
- Automation scripts to perform staged plan/apply in a sandbox (using ephemeral state) and to run health checks (see testing_and_health_checks).

Acceptance criteria (see acceptance_criteria):
acceptance_criteria: VSR schema committed to infra repo and referenced by docs
Initial registry entries for aws, azurerm, google providers and core modules
CI gate that validates provider/module constraint changes and fails PRs that violate policy
Automated canary job that can perform a staged terraform plan/apply in an isolated sandbox and run health checks
Operator playbook with explicit rollback criteria and contact escalation steps
Security review completed and any KMS/HSM impacts documented
tasks: Draft VSR JSON schema and vet with infra + SRE (Priya/Kevin)
Run compatibility matrix tests for current module/provider versions against tf 1.4.x and 1.5.x
Implement GH Action 'vsr-validate' to gate provider/module constraint changes
Build 'upgrade-canary' job that executes sandboxed apply and health checks
Author operator rolling-upgrade playbook and publish to Confluence
Add deprecation-signal automation (email + Slack + label) when registry entries age beyond 90d
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Registry bootstrapping: populate VSR and run CI validate on infra repo (non-blocking)
Phase 1 - Soft enforcement: CI validate blocks merges in infra repo only; informational for customer repos
Phase 2 - Auto-gated enforcement: enable CI validate in selected private-customer repos and require an upgrade-canary job for provider bumps
Phase 3 - Platform rollout: enable enforcement by default for new private deployments and provide migration tooling for existing repos
Phase 4 - Continuous testing: schedule weekly matrix runs for critical combos and auto-update compatibility_level
upgrade_matrix_summary: Matrix scope: combinations of terraform_version x provider_name x provider_version x module_name x module_version
Provider families: hashicorp/aws, hashicorp/azurerm, hashicorp/google, kubernetes
Compatibility outputs: tested_commit_sha, acceptance_status (pass/fail), test_notes, last_tested
Pinning policy summary: 'StrictPin' for Private with high compliance, 'SemVerPatch' for Dedicated, 'Flexible' for Hosted
testing_and_health_checks: Pre-upgrade: terraform plan dry-run + diff analyzer that flags breaking changes to resource lifecycle or provider defaults
Canary apply: deploy changes to an isolated small-scale sandbox that mirrors production networking and run infra smoke-tests
Runtime health checks: API latency SLO synthetic tests, route/egress connectivity checks, KV cache warm-up verification
Post-upgrade validation: run end-to-end customer flows (sample prompts that hit compute+storage), evaluate error-rate and token-latency regression thresholds
Automated rollback triggers: failed smoke-tests, increased 5xx error rate > 1% sustained for 5 minutes, or critical resource drift failures
rollback_strategy: Immediate plan: run terraform apply with previous state pin referenced by VSR and block canary promotion
Escalation: notify oncall SRE + infra owner, open an incident playbook ticket, and snapshot failing state
For long-running fails: schedule maintenance window and coordinate customer communications via success team
